candidate.mechanism: Cross-sectional open-interest growth: long the top quintile and short the bottom quintile of the prior-day log change in end-of-day open interest (contracts) among point-in-time eligible symbols of a pre-registered 72-symbol universe, entered at the UTC-day open and exited at the next UTC-day open, net of two 0.05% taker fees per position.
candidate.window_rationale: The two most recent complete calendar years covered by both the frozen 1h kline inventory (months 2021-12..2026-01) and the Data Vision metrics channel; each window is one calendar year so the quarter-stability gate has four quarters and the universe rule has a full preceding calendar year of volume.
candidate.calendar_novelty_claim: None. Both calendars were registered at cycle 5 and every historical calendar is treated as consumed by the policy. This contract claims only that the cycle-5 windows carry no computed outcome, so no outcome-conditioned choice was possible.

candidate.rule_level_claim: The only rule-level difference from cycle 5 is boundary-row handling. This is not claimed as novelty: it is a correction of a registered rule that misdescribed the data source, made under an explicit owner directive, at the cost of a new ordinal.

candidate.owner_directive_deviation: The directive asked for a cross-section "on the frozen 652-symbol inventory" with a 1 GiB acquisition cap. Daily metrics archives average 11.6 KB per symbol-day, so 652 symbols over two one-year windows (about 478,000 files, roughly 5.5 GB) cannot be acquired under the cap. The universe is therefore a pre-registered subset: the top 72 symbols of the frozen inventory by preceding-calendar-year quote volume with at least 300 complete kline days (universe-derivation.json; 104 distinct symbols across the two windows; 51,224 archives, 566.5 MB planned). Selection uses only pre-window volume, so it carries no look-ahead; it does restrict the claim to the liquid top of the cross-section, which is disclosed in the contract.

literature_boundary.source: Hong, H. and Yogo, M. (2012), What does futures market interest tell us about the macroeconomy and asset prices?, Journal of Financial Economics 105(3), 473-490
literature_boundary.relationship: Reports that growth in aggregate commodity futures open interest positively predicts commodity futures returns. The registered direction (long high open-interest growth, short low) is taken from that result; the crowding/unwind alternative (high open-interest growth followed by negative returns) is recorded as an untested non-claim and cannot be rescued after the outcome.
literature_boundary.crypto_specific_evidence: A bounded web search on 2026-09-02 for cross-sectional open-interest-growth return predictability on cryptocurrency perpetuals found no peer-reviewed cross-sectional result; the two nearest published items (net-short retail positioning and commercial-hedger positions predicting aggregate crypto returns) concern positioning, not open-interest growth, and are aggregate, not cross-sectional.
